 These applications coming on for admission this day, t  the following:
 ORDER

These are the second applications filed by the applicants under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.241/2023 dated 22.06.2023, registered at Police Station Parvati (Ashta), District Sehore (M.P.) fo r commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) of IPC and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Accused Aakash Malviya (applicant in M.Cr.C. No.54858 of 2023) is in detention since 17.07.2023 and accused Vinod (applicant M.Cr.C. No.54642 of 2023) is in detention since 06.09.2023.

2. Applicants' first bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide orders dated 23.08.2023 & 20.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.35681 of 2023 & M.Cr.C. No.46069 of 2023 respectively with liberty to revive the prayer for grant of bail after recording of prosecutrix evidence before the trial Court.

3. A s per the prosecution story, on 22.06.2023, 14 years old prosecutrix's father lodged an F.I.R.
about missing of her daughter.
F.I.R. was registered.
In the course of investigation, prosecutrix was recovered from possession of applicant Aakash Malviya.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed for commission of the aforesaid offence.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants have submitted that applicants have not committed any offence.
They are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix & her parents have already been examined before the trial Court.
They have turned hostile and have not supported the prosecution story.
Now, there is no possibility of influencing or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicants may be released on bail, pending the trial.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicants.
6. I have gone through the prosecutrix & her parents evidence recorded before the trial Court.
They have turned hostile and have not supported the prosecution story.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the change in the circumstances and other material placed on record, but without expressing anything on the merit, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicants is not warranted.
Consequently, these bail applications under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicants stand allowed.

7 . I t is directed that applicants - Aakash Malviya and Vinod be released on bail on their furnishing undertaking as aforesaid alongwith a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court,
for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

They shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE @shish Aakash Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62306945/
